title: U.S. House · North Carolina's 7th District
area: Southeastern North Carolina, including Wilmington and Fayetteville.

context.text: Incumbent David Rouzer (R) advanced from a contested Republican primary. Kimberly Hardy advanced from a canceled Democratic primary. Maad Abu-Ghazalah advanced from a canceled Libertarian primary. Independent Michael Henry did not make the general-election ballot.

candidates.name: David Rouzer

summary.text: David Rouzer is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in North Carolina's 7th Congressional District. A farm-raised Congressional and USDA staffer who ran a consulting business, he served in the North Carolina Senate from 2009 to 2012 and has represented the district in the U.S. House since 2015. He chairs the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee's Highways and Transit Subcommittee.

background.text: Born on a U.S. Army base in Landstuhl, Germany, in 1972; according to his House biography, he worked summers on his family's farm near Four Oaks, North Carolina.
Earned a bachelor's degree in agricultural business management, agricultural economics and chemistry from North Carolina State University in 1994.
Worked as a senior staffer for Sens. Jesse Helms and Elizabeth Dole, and later as assistant to the dean of North Carolina State University's College of Agriculture and Life Sciences.

Served as a presidential appointee at the U.S. Department of Agriculture (associate administrator, Rural Development), where his House biography says he helped manage a program-level budget of more than $1.2 billion.
Ran a small-business consulting firm, The Rouzer Company, and formed R&C Distributors, LLC, a fleet-products business, according to his House biography.

Elected to the North Carolina Senate in 2008 and served from 2009 to 2012 (Johnston and Wayne counties), including as co-chair of the Agriculture and Environment Committee and chair of the Senate Environmental Review Commission.
Narrowly lost the 2012 U.S. House race to Rep. Mike McIntyre (D); after McIntyre announced his retirement in January 2014, won the 2014 general election and took office in 2015.

In the 119th Congress, serves on the Agriculture, Transportation and Infrastructure, and Science, Space, and Technology committees, chairing the Highways and Transit Subcommittee. Won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary over David Buzzard, 80.5% to 19.5%.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture, the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, where he chairs the Highways and Transit Subcommittee and is vice chair of the General Farm Commodities, Risk Management, and Credit Subcommittee, and the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.

candidates.name: Kimberly Hardy
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from a canceled Democratic primary.

summary.text: Kimberly Hardy is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent David Rouzer in North Carolina's 7th Congressional District. A former school social worker with a Ph.D. in social work, she is a university social work professor and a vice chair of the North Carolina Democratic Party. She previously ran for the North Carolina House in 2020 and 2022.

background.text: Describes herself as raised by a police officer and a federal agent.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Morgan State University (1997), a master's in social work from Ohio State University, and a Ph.D. in social work from Morgan State University.
Worked as a school social worker before her academic career.

Has worked as an assistant professor of social work at the University of Connecticut (2010-2013) and the University of Saint Joseph (2013-2016), and later at Fayetteville State University, where Port City Daily reports she is an associate professor.
Ran as the Democratic nominee for North Carolina House District 43 (Fayetteville) in 2020, losing to Rep. Diane Wheatley (R) 51.8% to 48.2%; she also campaigned for the seat in 2022.
Has served as second vice chair of the North Carolina Democratic Party.
Announced her 2026 candidacy for the 7th District in summer 2025; the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary was canceled and she advanced to the general election.

priorities.text: Putting education first, saying the North Carolina General Assembly has left schools and students stuck in the Great Recession.

positions.summary: Lists expanding Medicaid among her top campaign priorities.

candidates.researchNotes: Hardy has not completed a 2026 Candidate Connection survey; positions are drawn from her 2020 survey, her most recent public statement of positions located within the research budget. She has not previously held elected office.

candidates.name: Maad Abu-Ghazalah
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from a canceled Libertarian Party primary.

summary.text: Maad Abu-Ghazalah is the Libertarian Party nominee in North Carolina's 7th Congressional District. He works as a consultant and holds degrees from the University of Notre Dame, the University of Virginia and Santa Clara University. In his Ballotpedia survey he describes himself as an anti-war, fiscally responsible candidate.

background.text: Attended King's School for high school.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Notre Dame (1983), a graduate degree from the University of Virginia (1985), and a law degree from Santa Clara University (1993).
Advanced to the November ballot after the March 3, 2026 Libertarian primary was canceled.

priorities.text: Ending U.S. involvement in foreign wars he says have nothing to do with national interest.
Balancing the federal budget and opposing what he calls irresponsible money printing.
Protecting civil liberties, particularly free speech.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions are drawn from Abu-Ghazalah's 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. He speaks generally against funding foreign wars, but since no source ties this directly to a specific issue key (e.g. Israel aid) by name, no formal Position entry was added for it; his general anti-war stance is captured only under priorities.
